## Historical audit — S0142

**Scope:** Only chunk 5 of 5 is visible. All citations below refer to S0142, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and renders are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and feedback — line 13, characters [419000,514658) | The visible instruction asks the student to compare a render with a reference and revise composition while preserving editable groups. A salon with a chaise is the inferred scene goal from the later program, not an independently viewed reference. This is guidance to the student; no teacher diagnosis or teacher-specific input is identified in this chunk. |
| Prior validation — line 13, [419000,514658) | Blender logs multiple `Rod` and `Ball` objects, completes 16/16 samples, saves step 2 `final.png` and `scene.blend`, and reports successful steps 1 and 2. This establishes a completed render and multiple Blender objects, not multiple distinct semantic objects or visual correctness. |
| Student assessment — line 15, [0,14787) | The student claims the chaise is too far right, its head too high, apron too open, pillow too rigid, floor too bright, stripes too strong and wall slope wrong. These are student diagnoses, not independent visual verification. The proposed response shifts the chaise, fills the apron, adjusts the pillow and crest, darkens the floor, changes stripes and rotates the room. |
| Program and execution — lines 15–16, [0,14787) and [0,15442) | The complete submitted program was passed to Blender as step 3. It specifies separate chaise, cane chair, curtains, paneled room and parquet assets; striped upholstery and bump materials; camera and lights. It attempts to transform and parent extra upholstery and panels to a chaise root, but actual part contact and successful parenting are not verified. Pillow rotation and chaise rotation/translation specify poses; their visual fit is unknown. Without step 2 code, exact changes relative to it cannot all be independently checked. |
| Outcome — lines 17–18, [0,1100) and [0,59) | Step 3 timed out after approximately 79.7 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and no image; step 2 was then selected. This is a **technical interruption**, not demonstrated algorithm failure or an empty patch. Step 2 had a formal successful-render indication, but overall scene correctness remains unknown. |

The fresh student session was read-only and recorded zero tool calls (line 14, [0,3843)); the visible comparison and program generation are student activity, but further autonomous exploration is not evidenced. The general instruction was present before the response, and the response follows its comparison/revision format; no receipt or adoption of any separate teacher feedback is established.

**Uncertainty and lessons:** The code provides evidence of intended materials, textures, multiple scene assets, assembly and lighting—not proof of their appearance, connections, occlusions, camera framing or render quality. The student’s wall-slope and brightness claims remain hypotheses. A transferable distinction is that a saved render and a selected prior step establish operational progress, not visual or geometric fidelity; the specific chaise offsets and room rotation are task-specific, unvalidated choices. Other chunks and images may contain relevant evidence, but are not inferred here.
